# backends/c/tests — W3C SCXML conformance harness for the C11 backend
# (RFC §5.J.1, downstream consumer).
#
# Sibling of `tests/` (the C++ AOT/Interpreter harness). C11 code is
# generated by `sce-codegen -l c11` into ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/
# generated/, then linked together with the per-fixture runner in
# `aot_tests/test_<NUM>.c` to produce one CTest binary per fixture.
#
# Per-fixture runners are intentionally minimal — `int main(void)`
# returning 0 on PASS and 1 on FAIL — because the C11 backend cannot
# pull in GoogleTest the way the C++ harness does. CTest treats the
# binary's exit status as the verdict, which is enough for AOT-only
# conformance (no in-test fixtures, no parametrised cases).

include(${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/SCEStaticW3CTest.cmake)
# Parallel CMake function for integration fixtures
# (`integration_resources/<stem>/<stem>.scxml` → `<output>/<stem>_sm.{h,c}`).
include(${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/SCEStaticIntegrationFixture.cmake)

set(SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated")
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}")

# Output dir for c11 integration-fixture codegen. Distinct from the
# W3C dir so build-system stale-tree detection treats W3C and integration
# trees as separate §6.2.6 drift contexts (RFC Q-2 parallel).
set(SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/integration_generated")
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}")

# Test-binary support helpers now live in backends/c/runtime as 4-tier-aligned
# libraries (see backends/c/runtime/CMakeLists.txt + ARCHITECTURE.md §"C11
# backend layering"). The W3C 204 conformance runner is the contract-test
# consumer of `sce_c_runtime_posix` (clock + http_client) and
# `sce_c_scripting` (lua_dom + http_lua bindings). Per-fixture link is
# wired in `sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test` below, gated by the existing
# NEEDS_{LUA,DOM,HTTP} flags.

# C11 fixture registry — extend as W3C category coverage grows.
# Each entry both (a) drives sce-codegen via the macro below and
# (b) lines up with `aot_tests/test_<NUM>.c` for the per-fixture runner.
set(W3C_C_AOT_TESTS "")
set(W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_LUA "")
set(W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_DOM "")
set(W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_HTTP "")
set(W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_INVOKE "")

sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(459 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 4.4: <log label="..." expr="..."> is observable side-effect only — pass / fail finals each carry an onentry log call that lowers to a `lua_eval_eventexpr` call (reused as the generic to-string helper) followed by `fprintf(stderr, "label: %s\n", buf)`; the boolean PASS path is independent of the log emit, so the new branch is verified by the C compiler's `-Werror` acceptance of the generated fprintf

sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(183 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.2.4: <send event=event1 idlocation=Var1> auto-stores the parser-generated sendid (`__send_N`) into the lua datamodel variable Var1 — the cond `typeof Var1 !== 'undefined'` reads Var1 as the bound string and routes to pass
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(332 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 5.10.1 + 6.2.4: <send target=!invalid event=foo idlocation=Var1> stores sendid in Var1 and raises error.execution with the same sendid on the event metadata — receiving transition reads `_event.sendid` (set via set_current_event's `_pending_send_id` lua global) into Var2 and the cond `Var1 === Var2` matches pass

sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(208 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}")  # W3C SCXML 6.3: <cancel sendid="foo"> removes the matching scheduled queue entry — event1 (id=foo, 1s) is cancelled, event2 (1.5s) fires first and routes to pass; otherwise the s0 wildcard `*` would catch event1 → fail. needs polling-driven _tick (test579 pattern)
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(210 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.3: <cancel sendidexpr="Var1"> evaluates Var1='foo' at cancel time via lua_eval_eventexpr → forwards the resulting string to scheduled_cancel; same observable shape as test208 (event1 cancelled, event2 fires first → pass). needs polling-driven _tick
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(330 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}")  # W3C SCXML 5.10: every dispatched event carries the required `name` field — s0's <raise event=foo> (internal queue) and s1's bare <send event=foo> (external queue) both round-trip the same name through the existing set_current_event lua chunk so the matching event="foo" transitions cover both queue paths

# W3C SCXML B.2 ECMAScript function-expression in value-expression context (test453): `<data id="var1" expr="function(invar) {return invar + 1;}"/>` previously lowered to `var1 = (function(invar) {return invar + 1\n})` — the trailing `}` was left raw, which is invalid Lua. transform_expression now invokes transform_function_syntax (mirroring the script pipeline's order at lua_transformer.rs:1822), so the same anonymous-function lowering that already worked inside `<script>` blocks now applies wherever an ECMAScript value-expression is accepted (cond, location/data/assign expr). Result: `var1 = (function(invar)  return invar + 1\n end)`, then `var1(2)` invokes natively and the cond `var1(2) == 3` matches.

# W3C SCXML 6.4 invoke — `<onentry><send target="#_parent">` in the child runs during the child's `enter_state_recursive` walk inside its `_init`, so parent_dispatch must be live BEFORE the entry walk rather than stamped after it. The codegen now emits `_init_with_parent` (parent_sm + dispatch parameters) for every child SM with `has_parent_communication=true` and removes the plain `_init` symbol for those SMs — the only call site is the parent's `execute_pending_invokes` helper. Child SMs whose only `<send target="#_parent">` lives in transition bodies (test226/240/241/243/244/245/276) take the same code path and behave identically because the post-init macrostep loop still drives those sends.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(191 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test191): minimal onentry `<send target="#_parent">` — child sub0 onentry sends `childToParent`, eventless transition enters subFinal. With parent_dispatch stamped before entry walk the send routes to the parent's external queue → s0→pass; without it the send drops, child reaches subFinal, done.invoke routes to `*` → fail. Pins the `_init_with_parent` ordering for the bare onentry-send shape.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(338 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 / 5.10.1 (test338): `<onentry>` of `<final id="sub0">` sends `event1` to `#_parent` (carrying the auto-generated invokeid). Parent captures `_event.invokeid` into Var2, compares against idlocation-bound Var1. Combines the onentry-stamp ordering with test228's invokeid plumbing — the send must reach the parent (live parent_dispatch during entry walk) AND carry the same id the parent stored at defer time.

# W3C SCXML 6.4 invoke — parent → child via `<send target="#_<invokeid>">`. Each invoke with an explicit `id="X"` exposes the embedded child's public `_raise_external_by_name` shim; the parent's send action codegen-resolves the `#_X` literal to the matching invoke at template time and emits a direct call. Combined with `_drive_active_children` (called from parent's `_step` after `execute_pending_invokes`), the dispatched event lands on the child's external queue and is drained on the same macrostep so the round-trip completes within the parent-side timeout.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(192 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test192): explicit `<invoke id="invokedChild">` + parent's `<send target="#_invokedChild" event="parentToChild">` from s01→s02 transition body. Child's onentry dispatches `childToParent` to parent; on receiving `parentToChild` the child transitions to subFinal with `<send target="#_parent" event="eventReceived">` before raising `done.invoke`. The verdict event must arrive before `done.invoke → fail` to drive parent → s02 → pass. Pins both the codegen-time `#_<id>` resolution and the macrostep-end child driving (without it the parent → child message would sit in the child's queue undrained until the 5 s timeout fires).

# W3C SCXML 6.2 invoke — child SCXML carries `<send delay="...">` in its own session. Parser's `parse_child_metadata` walks the child for any delayed send and stamps `child_needs_event_scheduler` on the invoke; `_drive_active_children` calls the child's `_tick` (which promotes elapsed scheduled entries) instead of just `_step` when the flag is on.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(207 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE)  # W3C SCXML 6.2 (test207): child schedules `event1` (1 s, sendid=foo) and `event2` (1.5 s) then immediately notifies parent via `childToParent`. Parent's `<cancel sendid="foo">` runs in parent's session and MUST NOT touch the child's scheduler — child's `event1` fires at 1 s, drives sub0→subFinal with `<send target="#_parent" event="pass">`, parent reaches pass. Pins per-session scheduler isolation + child `_tick` driven from `_drive_active_children`.

# W3C SCXML 3.4 / 6.4 invoke completion ordering — natural-final children run a `_finalize_session` exit walk so a final state's `<onexit><send target="#_parent">` fires BEFORE `done.invoke`; cancel-path children (parent state-exit destroys the invoke) get `parent_dispatch = NULL` BEFORE `_destroy`, dropping any onexit-emitted sends per W3C cancellation-drop semantics. Both helpers are gated on `child_has_send_to_parent` so test247-shape pure-final children skip both paths.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(236 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE)  # W3C SCXML 3.4 / 6.4 (test236): child = pure top-level `<final>` with `<onexit><send target="#_parent" event="childToParent">`. `_finalize_session` runs subFinal's onexit BEFORE `done.invoke` so parent transitions s0→s1 on childToParent and then s1→s2 on done.invoke (with `done.invoke → fail` at s0 level only matching if it arrives first). Parent's 2 s timeout drives s2→pass.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(252 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test252): parent's s01 onentry raises `foo`, the same macrostep transitions s01→s02 canceling the invoke. The cancel path NULLs the child's `parent_dispatch` before `_destroy`; child's `sub0 <onexit><send target="#_parent">` drops at the NULL guard. Parent's 1 s timeout fires unopposed → pass.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(347 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE)  # W3C SCXML C.1 (test347): both directions of `<send>` carry an explicit `type="http://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/#SCXMLEventProcessor"` — child→parent (#_parent) and parent→child (#_<invokeid>). Child sends `childRunning` to `#_parent` → parent's s01 captures `_event.origintype` into Var1 (must equal the SCXMLEventProcessor URI). s02 cond `Var1 == URI` dispatches `parentToChild` via `#_foo` → child's sub1 captures `_event.origintype` into Var2, then the URI cond fires `<send target="#_parent" event="success">`. Parent reaches pass. Verifies that both the cross-machine routing paths (`#_parent` and `#_<id>`) go through external-queue raises so the URI-seeded origintype is the same on both sides.

# W3C SCXML 6.2 + 6.4 invoke termination semantics — child's delayed `<send target="#_parent">` lives in the child's own `scheduled_queue` and is dropped silently when the child reaches `<final>` before the timer fires (W3C 6.2: "delayed send not delivered if session terminates"). The codegen lowers `target='#_parent' + delay` to `scheduled_push_parent` (new arm beside the existing immediate `#_parent` branch), and `_tick`'s promote loop reads the entry's `to_parent` discriminator before falling through to the local `raise_external` path. The unified scheduled_queue + flag layout keeps fire-time ordering single-source rather than splitting into a second buffer that would mirror cpp's per-child `parentSendScheduler_` shape.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(187 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE)  # W3C SCXML 6.2 (test187): child's onentry schedules `childToParent` to `#_parent` with delay=.5s, then takes the eventless `<transition target="subFinal"/>` straight to `<final>`. Child finalises during init's macrostep loop so `_tick` is never called on the dead child — the .5s entry is silently dropped. Parent's 1s `timeout` fires unopposed → s0→pass. If the delayed send leaked through, parent's `childToParent` transition would route to fail.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(215 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test215): `<invoke typeexpr="Var1">` with inline `<content><scxml initial="subFinal"><final/></scxml></content>`. The parser classifies this as a static invoke because `type=""` + non-empty inline content matches the `is_static_invoke` shape; the runtime typeexpr value never gates the spawn (cpp AOT codegen skips the eval too — same shape: `static_invoke=true`, child spawned unconditionally). Test passes because parent's onentry assigns `Var1='http://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/'` BEFORE the invoke is scheduled, so even if the codegen WERE evaluating typeexpr it would resolve to the SCXML processor URI and accept the spawn — both shapes converge on done.invoke → parent reaches pass.

The 2s entry never promotes, parent's s1 wildcard `event="*"` arm catches `timeout2` (1.5s) → pass. # W3C SCXML 6.4 invoke cancel-on-eventless-step — `<invoke>` is deferred until macrostep end, but the deferring state's `<onexit>` cancels its pending entry if the state is exited within the same macrostep. The c11 onexit hook calls `sce_invoke_pending_cancel_for_state` (backends/c/runtime/include/sce/invoke.h) before destroying any active children — so a state that defers an invoke and is exited via an eventless transition before macrostep end never spawns the child. Fixtures up to test239 carry one invoke per state and never exercise this path; test422 forces it with three invokes in one compound subtree where the middle child must be silently cancelled.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(422 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test422): three `<invoke>` declarations across compound subtree (s1, s11, s12). `_init`'s macrostep loop runs eventless transitions BEFORE `execute_pending_invokes`, so s11's eventless `<transition target="s12"/>` fires first, s11's onexit cancels s11's pending entry via `sce_invoke_pending_cancel_for_state`, and s12's onentry pushes its own. At macrostep end only s1 + s12 children spawn — their `invokeS1` / `invokeS12` increment Var1 to 2, and the 2s timeout's cond `Var1==2` routes to pass. SCE_MAX_INVOKES=4 covers the three-invoke working set; if the cancel hook were missed s11's `invokeS11` would route parent → fail.

# W3C SCXML 6.4 invoke namelist validation — the `<invoke namelist="...">` attribute names must each be declared in the PARENT's `<datamodel>`; if any name is missing, the processor MUST terminate the invocation and raise error.execution (cpp `InvokeExecutor::startInvoke` sce/src/runtime/InvokeExecutor.cpp:425-432 calls `destroySession + return ""` at runtime). c11 folds the membership check to a compile-time predicate: the codegen iterates `invoke_info.namelist.split()` against `model.variables | map(id)` and emits the error.execution raise + `continue` in `execute_pending_invokes` exactly when a name is undeclared. The skip-spawn branch sits before the child SM `_init` call so no resources are allocated. Verified non-regressing against test245 (declared namelist=Var2) — its error.execution emission count is unchanged.
# W3C SCXML 6.4 invoke autoforward — `<invoke autoforward="true">` requires the parent to ship an exact copy of every external event to the invoked process. cpp `StateMachine::processEvent` (sce/src/runtime/StateMachine.cpp:683) forwards via `getAutoForwardSessions + child->processEvent`; c11 mirrors with a per-SM `forward_to_autoforward_children` helper (state_machine.c.jinja2, gated on `model.has_autoforward_invoke`) that switches on the popped event enum and calls the active child's `_raise_external_by_name` shim with the parent-side event-name string. Platform events (done.*, error.*, cancel.invoke), the wildcard sentinel, and the empty-name placeholder are excluded — they are state-machine internal. Helper is only emitted when at least one invoke carries `autoforward="true"`, so existing fixtures stay byte-identical.
# W3C SCXML 6.4 invoke send-to-parent + finalize — `<send target="#_parent" event="X"><param name="K" expr="V"/></send>` in the child must carry param values to the parent's `_event.data.K`, AND each parent invoke's `<finalize>` body must run BEFORE transition selection so finalize-assigned parent vars are visible to the cond. cpp `StateMachine::processEvent` runs finalize via `InvokeExecutor::executeFinalize(invokeid)`; c11 mirrors via (a) parent_dispatch signature extended with `event_data` arg, (b) child's `<send target=#_parent>` with params codegen branch that builds a Lua-source table literal from each param expr (per-value formatter quotes strings, serialises numbers/booleans verbatim), (c) parent's `dispatch_external_by_name` shim copies `event_data` into `event_with_meta_t.data`, (d) parent's external dequeue runs `_event.data = (<table>)` then iterates registered finalize bodies, executing only those whose owning invoke's id matches `evt.invoke_id`. Per-invoke isolation pins test234's parallel-finalize fixture (each branch's finalize runs only for events from its own child).
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(234 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test234): parallel parent (p0 with p01+p02 regions) each carrying its own `<invoke>` with its own `<finalize>`. p01's child has `<final>` initial that sends `<send target=#_parent><param aParam=2/>`; p02's child has a 2 s `<send event="timeout">` (intra-child, not to parent) so p02 never raises a `<send target=#_parent>` event. The test233 per-invoke_id finalize-arm matches only the p01 invoke when `childToParent` arrives → p01 finalize sets Var1=2, p02 finalize stays unrun → Var2=1. Parent's `cond="Var1==2"` transitions to s1, then s1's eventless `cond="Var2==1"` routes to pass. Pins per-invoke isolation: a sibling invoke's finalize must NOT run on another sibling's events.

sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(233 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test233): child's `<final>` onentry sends `<send target="#_parent" event="childToParent"><param name="aParam" expr="2"/></send>`. Child-side codegen builds `{aParam = 2}` Lua source string in this child's lua_State, ships via parent_dispatch's `event_data` arg → parent shim memcpys into `evt.data` → parent's external dequeue hydrates `_event.data = ({aParam = 2})` → matches finalize-arm (active invoke + invoke_id match) → finalize body `Var1 = _event.data.aParam;` (transpiled to_lua_script) → Var1=2 → transition cond `Var1 == 2` matches → s0 → pass. Without finalize execution Var1 stays 1, cond fails, parent matches `<transition event="*"/>` → fail.

sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(229 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test229): child's onentry sends `childToParent` to `#_parent`. Parent's external dequeue hits the new `forward_to_autoforward_children` arm that calls `child._raise_external_by_name("childToParent")`. Post-step `_drive_active_children` drains the forwarded copy on the child's queue → child eventless-transitions to `subFinal` with `<send target="#_parent" event="eventReceived"/>` → parent's next external dequeue routes to pass. Without the forwarder the child's 3 s `timeout` would fire intra-child, `<transition event="*"/>` would route to `subFinal`, parent's `done.invoke → fail` arm would match.

sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(554 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4.1 (test554): `<invoke namelist="__undefined_variable_for_error__">` references a name not in the parent's `<datamodel>`. # W3C SCXML 6.2 + 5.4 manual-test automation lift — cpp `Test178.h` / `Test307.h` / `ScheduledAotTest`-shaped fixtures whose human-inspection contract collapses to "reach the `final` state, not `fail`". The W3C corpus marks these manual because the per-property observation (param key duplication, late-binding access timing, autoforward field equality, cancel-path onexit firing) lives in `<log>` output that no harness inspects automatically. cpp's runners already share this reduction — reaching the `final` state proves the upstream machinery (param emit, late binding, autoforward, cancel-path destroy) executed without diverting the SM into `fail` — so c11 mirrors the same single-bit verdict via the shared `_in_state(.., FINAL)` runner shape. No new template surface — these fixtures generate against the existing arms.

sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(230 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test230): autoforward field equality — child sends `childToParent` to parent, parent's `forward_to_autoforward_children` arm (test229) ships an exact copy back to the child via `_raise_external_by_name`, and both parent and child log every `_event` field for human inspection. The automated reduction is "reach the final state" — any divergence (forwarder filter dropping the event, child's wildcard misrouting, done.invoke arriving before the autoforward) routes the parent into `fail` via `<transition event="*"/>`.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(250 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4 (test250): cancel-path onexit — parent's s0 onentry sends `foo` then invokes a child with a 2 s timeout; the foo transition exits s0 cancelling the invoke. The W3C corpus marks this manual because the child's onexit emits `<log>` lines that no harness inspects (and the child cannot signal the parent post-cancel per W3C drop semantics). c11's `destroy_active_children` cancel-path (test237/252 already pin) frees the child SM and the parent reaches FINAL — the conformance bit.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(307 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 5.2.2 (test307): `binding="late"` access semantics — s0 logs Var1 before s1 declares it; s1 logs Var1.foo (missing property) after binding. Both accesses MUST yield ECMAScript undefined silently (no error.execution). # W3C SCXML 6.4.3 / 6.4.4 hybrid invoke — `<invoke srcexpr>` + `<invoke><content expr>` runtime evaluation. cpp uses a pure-AOT pattern with a trivial immediate-final stub child (`test{N}_hybrid{idx}.scxml`, written by sce-build's `generate_hybrid_child_scxmls`). The eval runs at macrostep end on the parent's lua_State for validation only — the result is intentionally not consumed because the W3C contract checks evaluation timing, not the value. Both fixtures' actual children (`test216sub1.scxml` is `<final/>`-only; test530's inline scxml is `<scxml><final/></scxml>`) are immediate-final, so the stub is observationally identical for the contract being tested.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(216 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4.3 (test216): `<invoke srcexpr="Var1">` runtime evaluation — Var1 reassigned in onentry to the child path, codegen lowers a luaL_dostring eval-validation gate then spawns the pre-generated `test216_hybrid0` stub child. cpp `test216_sm.inl:166-185` is the equivalent pure-AOT pattern.
sce_generate_static_w3c_c_test(530 "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}" NEEDS_INVOKE NEEDS_LUA)  # W3C SCXML 6.4.4 (test530): `<invoke><content expr="Var1"/></invoke>` runtime evaluation — Var1 reassigned in onentry from integer 1 to a literal SCXML scriptlet, codegen lowers a luaL_dostring eval-validation gate then spawns the pre-generated `test530_hybrid0` stub child (byte-equivalent to the original inline `<scxml><final/></scxml>`). cpp `test530_sm.inl:166-185` is the equivalent pattern.

# One CTest binary per fixture. Compiled with the C11 dialect explicitly so
# `SCE_STATIC_ASSERT`'s C11 lowering and stdint/stdbool are first-class
# regardless of the compiler's default standard. Lua54 is linked only into fixtures flagged
# NEEDS_LUA so datamodel-less fixtures preserve their MCU-relevant
# zero-deps profile.
# The runners link the SCE-shipped POSIX platform impl for clock.h and
# http_client.h, so they exist only when it is built. A bare-metal
# consumer opting out still gets the freestanding forge and EventSchema
# fixtures below, which link neither it nor a script engine.
if(SCE_C_RUNTIME_POSIX)
    foreach(TEST_NUM ${W3C_C_AOT_TESTS})
        # A fixture flagged NEEDS_LUA / NEEDS_DOM / NEEDS_HTTP reaches lua54
        # or sce_c_scripting below, and both are built only under
        # SCE_ENABLE_LUA. Skipping just those keeps the datamodel-less
        # fixtures — the MCU-relevant zero-deps profile this loop's link
        # flags exist to preserve — running without a script engine.
        if(NOT SCE_ENABLE_LUA
           AND (${TEST_NUM} IN_LIST W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_LUA
                OR ${TEST_NUM} IN_LIST W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_DOM
                OR ${TEST_NUM} IN_LIST W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_HTTP))
            continue()
        endif()
        set(_runner "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/aot_tests/test_${TEST_NUM}.c")
        set(_generated "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}/test${TEST_NUM}_sm.c")
        set(_target "sce_c_w3c_test_${TEST_NUM}")
        # W3C SCXML 6.4: per-test invoke child sources. Empty for fixtures that
        # carry no `<invoke>` (the variable is unset / empty list); fixtures
        # marked NEEDS_INVOKE see the sce-build-extracted
        # `__sce_synth_invoke__*_sm.c` translation units staged into the
        # binary so child SM types are linked into the parent's _sm.c.
        set(_child_sources "${W3C_C_AOT_TEST_${TEST_NUM}_CHILD_SOURCES}")

        add_executable(${_target} ${_runner} ${_generated} ${_child_sources})
        target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE sce_c_runtime sce_c_runtime_posix)
        target_include_directories(${_target} PRIVATE "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}")
        # Each arm names SCE_ENABLE_LUA alongside its fixture flag. The
        # `continue()` above already means a script-engine fixture has no
        # target here without it, so these conjuncts change no build — what
        # they change is that the dependency is stated where the library is
        # named, which is where a reader and the guard-scope gate look.
        if(SCE_ENABLE_LUA AND ${TEST_NUM} IN_LIST W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_LUA)
            target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE lua54)
        endif()
        if(SCE_ENABLE_LUA AND ${TEST_NUM} IN_LIST W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_DOM)
            # sce_c_base provides the freestanding DOM parser; sce_c_scripting
            # adds the Lua binding (which needs lua54 — pulled transitively).
            target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE sce_c_base sce_c_scripting)
        endif()
        if(SCE_ENABLE_LUA AND ${TEST_NUM} IN_LIST W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_HTTP)
            # sce_c_runtime_posix provides http_client; sce_c_scripting adds
            # the Lua binding for HTTP fixtures.
            target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE sce_c_scripting)
        endif()
        set_target_properties(${_target} PROPERTIES
            C_STANDARD 11
            C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON
            C_EXTENSIONS OFF
        )

        add_test(NAME w3c_c_aot_${TEST_NUM} COMMAND ${_target})
        set_tests_properties(w3c_c_aot_${TEST_NUM} PROPERTIES
            TIMEOUT 30
            LABELS "w3c;c11;aot"
        )
        if(${TEST_NUM} IN_LIST W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_HTTP)
            set_tests_properties(w3c_c_aot_${TEST_NUM} PROPERTIES
                FIXTURES_REQUIRED w3c_c_http_server
            )
        endif()
    endforeach()
else()
    list(LENGTH W3C_C_AOT_TESTS _sce_c_w3c_skipped)
    message(STATUS
        "SCE_C_RUNTIME_POSIX=OFF — skipping ${_sce_c_w3c_skipped} W3C "
        "C11 conformance runner(s); they link sce_c_runtime_posix for "
        "clock + http_client.")
endif()

# Every fixture below links sce_c_runtime_posix and lua54, so the whole
# block is bounded by the two options that build them.

    # W3C SCXML 6.4 autoforward carries `done.invoke.<id>`. Appendix D
    # `mainEventLoop` forwards every event dequeued from the external queue to each
    # autoforward child and excludes only the cancel event; §6.4.2 puts
    # `done.invoke.<id>` on that queue. Observing it needs two concurrent invokes,
    # which is why no IRP test covers it.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(autoforward_done_invoke "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
        SYNTH_INVOKE_CHILDREN inv_watch inv_short

    # W3C SCXML 6.4: the negative half of the same loop. The internal drain has
    # no forwarding step, so `error.execution` (6.2, unsupported `<send>` type)
    # must never reach an autoforward child — excluded by the queue it was
    # raised onto, not by a filter that recognises its name.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(autoforward_internal_queue "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"

    # W3C SCXML 6.4: *where* in the loop the forward happens. Appendix D puts it
    # one statement after `externalQueue.dequeue()`, and 6.4.2 in prose at the
    # point at which the parent removes the event from the external event queue.
    # The two fixtures above are blind to this by construction — queue order
    # alone cannot tell the enqueue from the dequeue, so the parent marks the
    # child directly with `<send target="#_inv_probe">` from a transition body.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(autoforward_dequeue_point "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"

    # W3C SCXML Appendix D: *when* the invokes start relative to the external
    # dequeue. mainEventLoop completes the macrostep on eventless and internal
    # transitions alone, runs invoke(inv), and only then reaches
    # externalQueue.dequeue(). The fixture above cannot see this axis — its child
    # opens the exchange, so it is alive before anything is queued; here the
    # parent queues for itself in onentry and the child starts second.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(invoke_precedes_external_dequeue "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
        SYNTH_INVOKE_CHILDREN inv_watch
    )

    add_executable(sce_c_integration_invoke_precedes_external_dequeue
        integration/test_invoke_precedes_external_dequeue.c
        ${INTEGRATION_C_TEST_invoke_precedes_external_dequeue_SOURCES}

        "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
    )
    set_target_properties(sce_c_integration_invoke_precedes_external_dequeue PROPERTIES
        C_STANDARD 11
        C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON
        C_EXTENSIONS OFF

        TIMEOUT 30
        LABELS "integration;c11;aot"
    )

    # W3C SCXML Appendix D: the same order, reached mid-run. statesToInvoke is
    # filled by enterStates inside microstep, so a state entered by an external
    # event's transition arms an invoke that must start before the next event is
    # dequeued. The fixture above enters its invoking state at initialization and
    # cannot see an engine that drains the external queue to exhaustion per step.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(invoke_precedes_dequeue_midrun "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
        SYNTH_INVOKE_CHILDREN inv_watch

    # W3C SCXML 3.7: a <final> nested inside a compound state completes that
    # state, not the session — Appendix D enterStates ends the session only when
    # the final's parent is the <scxml> element. The fixture rests in the nested
    # final so the completion predicate is sampled while the machine is still live.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(nested_final_not_terminal "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}")

    # W3C SCXML 3.4 + 3.7: a <parallel> completes when every region reaches a
    # <final>, and that raises done.state.<parallel>. A parallel owns no <final>
    # directly, so a rule registering the event by walking to a final's parent
    # never reaches it — while this backend's emitter raises it from the
    # grandparent. The generated code then named an undeclared enumerator, which
    # is a compile failure: building this target is most of the gate.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(parallel_completion_raises_done_state "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}")

    add_executable(sce_c_integration_parallel_completion_raises_done_state
        integration/test_parallel_completion_raises_done_state.c
        ${INTEGRATION_C_TEST_parallel_completion_raises_done_state_SOURCES}

    set_tests_properties(c11_integration_parallel_completion_raises_done_state PROPERTIES
        TIMEOUT 30
        LABELS "integration;c11;aot"
    )

    # W3C SCXML 3.4 + 3.7, the other half: declared is not delivered. The
    # fixture above carries no listener on purpose — a transition's `event`
    # attribute registers the name by itself, which would leave it unable to
    # fail — so what it proves is that this backend DECLARES the enumerator.
    # An emitter that names it and never raises it still compiles. This one
    # listens, and its verdict is a top-level <final> nothing else can reach.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(parallel_done_state_is_delivered "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}")

    add_executable(sce_c_integration_parallel_done_state_is_delivered

    # W3C SCXML 3.4: one event can enable a transition in more than one region
    # of a <parallel>, and every such region takes its own in the same
    # microstep. The fixture is asymmetric on purpose — one region's transition
    # is an external self-transition, whose domain is a proper ancestor and
    # never the state itself; answering otherwise made the exit set name the
    # enclosing <parallel> and preempt the sibling region.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(parallel_regions_take_own_transitions "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}")

    # W3C SCXML 6.4.1: an <invoke> whose `type` names no processor this platform
    # implements is valid SCXML that must raise error.execution — not a document to
    # reject at build time. C11 reaches that raise through three gates the other
    # backends do not share (the entry-action switch, the scxml_family include
    # guards, and an execute_pending_invokes arm the `| scxml` filter skips), so
    # the fixture is the only thing that proves all three are open.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(invoke_unsupported_type "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}")

    # W3C SCXML 5.5 + 6.3.1: donedata rides done.invoke.<id> wherever the child
    # reaches its final state, not only where it finalises during start-up. The
    # donedata_local_invoke fixture pins the payload shapes on a child that is
    # already final at invoke time and is blind to this; here the child answers
    # an event first and reaches <final> two macrosteps in.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(donedata_late_completion "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"

    # W3C SCXML 6.2: a <send> carries its <param> payload on both the paths that
    # had no runtime witness — from a datamodel="null" child (which needs no
    # script engine, so param emission must be judged per send rather than per

    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(send_param_payload "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"

    # W3C SCXML C.1: the origin of a delivered event is the location the
    # sending session published for the SCXML Event I/O Processor, and that
    # location is a usable <send> target. The IRP suite checks neither half
    # across sessions — test336 and test350 both send to the session they
    # already are — so this fixture puts a peer session on the other end.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(event_origin_is_a_location "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
        SYNTH_INVOKE_CHILDREN inv_peer

        LABELS "integration;c11;aot"

    # W3C SCXML 5.10: `_sessionid` is the id of a session, not of a document.
    # Two children run at once and report the id each was issued; a processor
    # that hands both the same value publishes one address for two sessions
    # (C.1.1), and a `<send>` to either reaches both. Every corpus test that
    # reaches `_sessionid` runs a single session, so none of them can ask.
    sce_generate_static_integration_c_test(session_ids_are_distinct "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
        SYNTH_INVOKE_CHILDREN inv_a inv_b
    )

    add_executable(sce_c_integration_session_ids_are_distinct
        integration/test_session_ids_are_distinct.c
        ${INTEGRATION_C_TEST_session_ids_are_distinct_SOURCES}
    )
    target_link_libraries(sce_c_integration_session_ids_are_distinct PRIVATE
        sce_c_runtime sce_c_runtime_posix lua54
    )
    target_include_directories(sce_c_integration_session_ids_are_distinct PRIVATE
        "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
    )
    set_target_properties(sce_c_integration_session_ids_are_distinct PROPERTIES
        C_STANDARD 11
        C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON
        C_EXTENSIONS OFF
    )
    add_test(NAME c11_integration_session_ids_are_distinct
        COMMAND sce_c_integration_session_ids_are_distinct
    )
    set_tests_properties(c11_integration_session_ids_are_distinct PROPERTIES
        TIMEOUT 30
        LABELS "integration;c11;aot"
    )
else()
    message(STATUS
        "skipping the c11 integration fixtures — they link "
        "sce_c_runtime_posix and lua54, which SCE_C_RUNTIME_POSIX / "
        "SCE_ENABLE_LUA do not build in this configuration.")
endif()

# ─── forge buffer pool: RFC §synth-5-E slot FSM, exercised ──────────
#
# The pool header had no compile target anywhere in the tree — its only
# verification was a text grep over the emitted source, and a byte
# golden proves determinism rather than correctness. Compiling it is
# half the gap; the other half is that a header can compile and still
# hand out a slot twice. This target runs the FSM: acquire/return,
# free_count, payload round-trip, exhaustion, and the three separate
# guards on a bad handle (index, pool-state comparison, CPU-ownership
# tag) — each reached by a shape that the other two cannot reject, so
# no guard is vouched for by a sibling.
set(_FP_FIXTURE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/forge/resources/buffer_pool_ast_export_min.scxml")
set(_FP_HEADER "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}/buffer_pool_ast_export_min.h")
add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_FP_HEADER}"
    COMMAND ${SCE_CODEGEN_ENV} "${SCE_CODEGEN}" generate "${_FP_FIXTURE}"
            -l c -o "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
            --write-deps "${_FP_HEADER}.d"
    DEPENDS "${_FP_FIXTURE}" "${SCE_CODEGEN}"
    DEPFILE "${_FP_HEADER}.d"
    COMMENT "Generating forge buffer-pool fixture: buffer_pool_ast_export_min.h"
    VERBATIM
)
add_custom_target(sce_c_forge_buffer_pool_header DEPENDS "${_FP_HEADER}")

add_executable(sce_c_integration_forge_buffer_pool
    integration/test_forge_buffer_pool.c
)
add_dependencies(sce_c_integration_forge_buffer_pool sce_c_forge_buffer_pool_header)
target_include_directories(sce_c_integration_forge_buffer_pool PRIVATE
    "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/backends/c/forge-runtime/include"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/backends/c/runtime/include"
)
# The pool is header-only `static inline` over file-scope storage, so
# there is no runtime library to link — the MCU single-TU premise.
target_compile_options(sce_c_integration_forge_buffer_pool PRIVATE
    -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wpedantic
    -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wshadow -Wcast-align
)
set_target_properties(sce_c_integration_forge_buffer_pool PROPERTIES
    C_STANDARD 11
    C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON
    C_EXTENSIONS OFF
)
add_test(NAME c11_integration_forge_buffer_pool
    COMMAND sce_c_integration_forge_buffer_pool
)
set_tests_properties(c11_integration_forge_buffer_pool PROPERTIES
    TIMEOUT 30
    LABELS "integration;c11;aot"
)

# ─── forge bounded collection: RFC §synth-5-D, exercised ────────────
#
# This one *was* compiled before — but only because an unrelated keyexpr
# fixture happens to emit a collection, so `c7_keyexpr_field_match`
# dragged it through a compiler as a side effect. That coverage vanishes
# the moment the keyexpr fixture changes, and it never covered behaviour.
#
# The property under test is the generation-tagged handle: a handle to a
# slot that has since been freed and *reused* must not resolve. A
# slot-index-only handle passes every simpler check and then silently
# addresses the wrong element.
#
# Three fixtures because the collection's element type is itself a forge
# document: `subscription_entry` (element) → `local_sub_table`
# (collection). Generating the collection alone fails on a missing
# element header.
set(_BC_FIXTURE_DIR "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/forge/resources")
set(_BC_ENTRY_HEADER "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}/subscription_entry.h")
set(_BC_TABLE_HEADER "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}/local_sub_table.h")
add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_BC_ENTRY_HEADER}"
    COMMAND ${SCE_CODEGEN_ENV} "${SCE_CODEGEN}" generate "${_BC_FIXTURE_DIR}/subscription_entry.scxml"
            -l c -o "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
            --write-deps "${_BC_ENTRY_HEADER}.d"
    DEPENDS "${_BC_FIXTURE_DIR}/subscription_entry.scxml" "${SCE_CODEGEN}"
    DEPFILE "${_BC_ENTRY_HEADER}.d"
    COMMENT "Generating forge bounded-collection element: subscription_entry.h"
    VERBATIM
)
add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_BC_TABLE_HEADER}"
    COMMAND ${SCE_CODEGEN_ENV} "${SCE_CODEGEN}" generate "${_BC_FIXTURE_DIR}/local_sub_table.scxml"
            -l c -o "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
            --write-deps "${_BC_TABLE_HEADER}.d"
    DEPENDS "${_BC_FIXTURE_DIR}/local_sub_table.scxml" "${_BC_ENTRY_HEADER}" "${SCE_CODEGEN}"
    DEPFILE "${_BC_TABLE_HEADER}.d"
    COMMENT "Generating forge bounded collection: local_sub_table.h"
    VERBATIM
)
add_custom_target(sce_c_forge_bounded_collection_headers DEPENDS "${_BC_TABLE_HEADER}")

add_executable(sce_c_integration_forge_bounded_collection
    integration/test_forge_bounded_collection.c
)
add_dependencies(sce_c_integration_forge_bounded_collection sce_c_forge_bounded_collection_headers)
target_include_directories(sce_c_integration_forge_bounded_collection PRIVATE
    "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/backends/c/forge-runtime/include"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/backends/c/runtime/include"
)
target_compile_options(sce_c_integration_forge_bounded_collection PRIVATE
    -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wpedantic
    -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wshadow -Wcast-align
)
set_target_properties(sce_c_integration_forge_bounded_collection PROPERTIES
    C_STANDARD 11
    C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON
    C_EXTENSIONS OFF
)
add_test(NAME c11_integration_forge_bounded_collection
    COMMAND sce_c_integration_forge_bounded_collection
)
set_tests_properties(c11_integration_forge_bounded_collection PROPERTIES
    TIMEOUT 30
    LABELS "integration;c11;aot"
)

# ─── EventSchema native lowering fixture (NL→IR C1 Path A, RFC §10.4 step 5) ─
#
# Proves the C11 backend's native typed `_event.data` lowering at runtime
# (the downstream value path): a guard `_event.data.elapsed_ms === 0`
# lowers to a tagged-union comparison with NO script engine, and the typed
# inject seam `..._raise_external_typed` drives it. Generation runs directly
# from the read-only resource dir (NOT via the staging helper) so the
# `<sce:import kind="event-schema">` sibling resolves relative to the
# importing statechart's own directory.
#
# MCU-clean gate: the target links NO runtime library — the datamodel-less
# native path is fully self-contained (only header-only `sce/types.h`
# constants), so a successful link is the no-Lua / no-script-engine proof
# for a bare-metal target.
set(_ES_FIXTURE_ROOT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/integration_resources/event_schema_native")
set(_ES_PARENT_SOURCE "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}/event_schema_native_sm.c")
set(_ES_PARENT_HEADER "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}/event_schema_native_sm.h")
add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_ES_PARENT_SOURCE}"
    COMMAND ${SCE_CODEGEN_ENV} "${SCE_CODEGEN}" generate
            "${_ES_FIXTURE_ROOT}/event_schema_native.scxml"
            -l c11 -o "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
            --write-deps "${_ES_PARENT_SOURCE}.d"
    DEPENDS "${_ES_FIXTURE_ROOT}/event_schema_native.scxml"
            "${_ES_FIXTURE_ROOT}/schema_job_completed.scxml"
            "${SCE_CODEGEN}"
    DEPFILE "${_ES_PARENT_SOURCE}.d"
    BYPRODUCTS "${_ES_PARENT_HEADER}"
    COMMENT "Generating C11 EventSchema native-lowering fixture: event_schema_native_sm.{h,c}"
    VERBATIM
)

add_executable(sce_c_integration_event_schema_native
    integration/test_event_schema_native.c
    "${_ES_PARENT_SOURCE}"
    "${_ES_PARENT_HEADER}"
)
# Intentionally NO target_link_libraries: the native value path links zero
# runtime — that is the MCU-clean acceptance proof (RFC §10.4 step 5).
target_include_directories(sce_c_integration_event_schema_native PRIVATE
    "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/backends/c/runtime/include"
)
set_target_properties(sce_c_integration_event_schema_native PROPERTIES
    C_STANDARD 11
    C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON
    C_EXTENSIONS OFF
)
add_test(NAME c11_integration_event_schema_native
    COMMAND sce_c_integration_event_schema_native
)
set_tests_properties(c11_integration_event_schema_native PROPERTIES
    TIMEOUT 30
    LABELS "integration;c11;aot"
)

# ─── BasicHTTP fixture: standalone Node server lifecycle ────────────
#
# The W3C SCXML C.2 corpus addresses `http://localhost:8080/test` on the
# fixture-side and expects a server to echo events back. The cpp side's
# `w3c_test_cli` runs the same expectation via in-process orchestration
# (`tests/w3c/standalone_http_server.js` spawned by the WASM polyfill;
# native cpp uses the in-process httplib server). C11 fixtures run as
# bare ctest executables with no orchestrator, so without this ctest
# FIXTURES_SETUP every NEEDS_HTTP `w3c_c_aot_<N>` test would hit a dead
# socket and time out in `sce_test_http_post`.
#
# The setup arm launches `node tests/w3c/standalone_http_server.js
# 8080 /test`, waits for the `[READY]` line on stdout (capped at 5s),
# and records the pid. The cleanup arm reads the pid and SIGTERMs it
# (KILL fallback after 2s). Both arms are idempotent so a partial-run
# `ctest -R w3c_c_aot_513` followed by another ctest invocation does
# not stack server instances.
# The two options are named alongside the fixture list because the list
# is populated by the registrations above, which run whether or not the
# runners are built. Without them a bare-metal or script-engine-less
# configuration registers a server fixture that no test can require —
# inert, since ctest starts a fixture only on demand, but it reads in
# `ctest -N` as coverage that is not there.
if(SCE_C_RUNTIME_POSIX AND SCE_ENABLE_LUA AND W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_HTTP)
    find_program(SCE_TEST_NODE_EXECUTABLE node)
    if(SCE_TEST_NODE_EXECUTABLE)
        set(_http_fixture_pid "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/w3c_http_server.pid")
        set(_http_fixture_sh "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/w3c/http_server_fixture.sh")
        set(_http_server_js "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/w3c/standalone_http_server.js")

        add_test(NAME w3c_c_http_server_setup
            COMMAND bash "${_http_fixture_sh}" start
                "${SCE_TEST_NODE_EXECUTABLE}" "${_http_server_js}"
                8080 /test "${_http_fixture_pid}"
        )
        set_tests_properties(w3c_c_http_server_setup PROPERTIES
            FIXTURES_SETUP w3c_c_http_server
            TIMEOUT 15
            LABELS "w3c;c11;aot;fixture"
        )

        add_test(NAME w3c_c_http_server_cleanup
            COMMAND bash "${_http_fixture_sh}" stop "${_http_fixture_pid}"
        )
        set_tests_properties(w3c_c_http_server_cleanup PROPERTIES
            FIXTURES_CLEANUP w3c_c_http_server
            TIMEOUT 10
            LABELS "w3c;c11;aot;fixture"
        )
    else()
        message(WARNING
            "node not found on PATH; W3C SCXML C.2 BasicHTTP fixtures "
            "(${W3C_C_AOT_TESTS_NEEDS_HTTP}) will time out at runtime. "
            "Install Node.js or use ctest -E w3c_c_aot_'(201|509|510|513|"
            "518|519|520|522|531|532|534|567)$' to skip.")
    endif()
endif()

# sce_c_scripting carries the lua_dom binding this suite reads through,
# and it is built only under SCE_ENABLE_LUA.
if(SCE_ENABLE_LUA)
    # ─── DOM helper unit tests ──────────────────────────────────────────
    #
    # Coverage for the full pugixml feature set (DOCTYPE / CDATA / entity
    # decoding / mixed text PCDATA) that the W3C SCXML B.2 corpus does not
    # force. Without these the additions to backends/c/tests/support/dom.c are
    # unconsumed; the unit suite is the first reader and pins the parser's
    # `parse_default`-equivalent behaviour against drift.
    add_executable(sce_c_dom_unit_test unit/dom_test.c)
    target_link_libraries(sce_c_dom_unit_test PRIVATE sce_c_runtime sce_c_base sce_c_scripting)
    set_target_properties(sce_c_dom_unit_test PROPERTIES
        C_STANDARD 11
        C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON
        C_EXTENSIONS OFF
    )
    add_test(NAME c11_unit_dom COMMAND sce_c_dom_unit_test)
    set_tests_properties(c11_unit_dom PROPERTIES
        TIMEOUT 10
        LABELS "unit;c11"
    )
else()
    message(STATUS
        "skipping c11_unit_dom — it links sce_c_scripting, which "
        "SCE_ENABLE_LUA does not build in this configuration.")
endif()

# Linked against the POSIX platform impl (the client under test) and
# sce_c_scripting (the http_lua binding), so this binary exists only
# when both are built.
if(SCE_C_RUNTIME_POSIX AND SCE_ENABLE_LUA)
    # ─── HTTP client unit tests ────────────────────────────────────────
    #
    # Coverage for the host-side HTTP/1.1 client + JSON response extractor
    # (backends/c/tests/support/http_client.{c,h}). The W3C SCXML C.2 corpus
    # only exercises the happy path against the standalone Node server;
    # these unit tests force edge cases the corpus does not (URL parsing
    # rejections, percent-encoding overflow, depth-counted JSON object
    # capture with embedded `}`, `\uXXXX` UTF-8 unescape) plus a single
    # end-to-end POST round-trip against an in-process loopback server
    # (TCP 127.0.0.1, OS-assigned port, single-shot accept thread). pthread
    # link is local to this binary — sce_c_test_http_support stays free of
    # threading deps so fixture binaries that only call the synchronous
    # POST API do not pull pthread either.
    find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
    add_executable(sce_c_http_client_unit_test unit/http_client_test.c)
    target_link_libraries(sce_c_http_client_unit_test
        PRIVATE
            sce_c_runtime
            sce_c_runtime_posix
            sce_c_scripting
            Threads::Threads
    )
    set_target_properties(sce_c_http_client_unit_test PROPERTIES
        C_STANDARD 11
        C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON
        C_EXTENSIONS OFF
    )
    add_test(NAME c11_unit_http_client COMMAND sce_c_http_client_unit_test)
    set_tests_properties(c11_unit_http_client PROPERTIES
        TIMEOUT 30
        LABELS "unit;c11"
        # In-process loopback pthread server with a 5s client recv timeout —
        # CPU-heavy peers under `ctest -j` starve scheduling and flake the
        # bound. Force serial so the round-trip runs unimpeded.
        RUN_SERIAL TRUE
    )
else()
    message(STATUS
        "skipping c11_unit_http_client — it links sce_c_runtime_posix "
        "and sce_c_scripting, which SCE_C_RUNTIME_POSIX / SCE_ENABLE_LUA "
        "do not build in this configuration.")
endif()

# ─── C++ consumption gate ───────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Every header the C11 backend publishes (`backends/c/runtime/include/sce`,
# `backends/c/forge-runtime/include/sce/forge`) and every header it
# generates opens `#ifdef __cplusplus extern "C"`. That is a contract
# with C++ consumers — an AP-side application links the same generated
# machine an MCU compiles — and nothing checked it until this gate.
#
# It was not being met. `_Static_assert` is a C11 keyword with no C++
# spelling, and it appeared in `sce/sample.h` and in every generated
# `_sm.h`, so a C++ translation unit including any of them failed to
# parse. GCC rejected them; Clang accepted them as an extension and
# rejected them again under `-Werror`. The headers are now written
# through `SCE_STATIC_ASSERT` (`sce/portability.h`), and this gate is
# what keeps them that way — a fix without it regresses the first time
# someone writes the keyword back.
#
# The gate scans directories at test time rather than taking a
# registered file list, so a header added later is covered without
# anyone remembering to add it, and a root that resolves to zero
# headers fails rather than passing over an empty set.
#
# That last property is why the W3C tree is named conditionally. Nothing
# consumes its codegen when the runners are not built, so ninja never
# runs it and the directory stays empty — which the gate reports as a
# broken scan, correctly, because it cannot tell "nobody generated this"
# from "the scan lost its root". Naming only the trees this
# configuration populates keeps the floor meaningful instead of
# weakening it to tolerate emptiness.
set(_sce_cxx_scan_roots
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/backends/c/runtime/include/sce"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/backends/c/forge-runtime/include/sce/forge"
    "${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}"
)
if(SCE_C_RUNTIME_POSIX)
    list(APPEND _sce_cxx_scan_roots "${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}")
endif()
list(JOIN _sce_cxx_scan_roots "|" _sce_cxx_scan_roots)

add_test(NAME c11_headers_are_cxx_consumable
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND}
        -DSCE_CXX_COMPILER=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}
        -DSCE_CXX_STANDARD=17
        -DSCE_SCAN_ROOTS=${_sce_cxx_scan_roots}
        -DSCE_INCLUDE_DIRS=${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/backends/c/runtime/include|${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/backends/c/forge-runtime/include|${SCE_C_GENERATED_DIR}|${SCE_C_INTEGRATION_GENERATED_DIR}|${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/third_party/lua/src
        -DSCE_WORK_DIR=${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/cxx_consumption
        -P ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cxx_consumption_gate.cmake
)
set_tests_properties(c11_headers_are_cxx_consumable PROPERTIES
    TIMEOUT 300
    LABELS "unit;c11"
)

# ============================================================
# Aggregate build target for the whole C11 test surface.
# ============================================================
#
# `ctest -L c11` runs 218 tests across 215 separate executables. Building
# them needs a target: `cmake --build build` with no target builds the
# entire project — the C++ engine, mesh, forge, the examples — which is
# most of the cost for a lane that only exercises the C backend, and the
# C backend links none of it (`sce_c_runtime` + `sce_c_runtime_posix`,
# plus lua54 / sce_c_base / sce_c_scripting where a fixture needs them).
#
# The dependency list is derived from the directory rather than written
# out. A hand-maintained list of 215 names would be wrong the first time
# someone adds a fixture and forgets it, and the failure mode is the one
# this whole lane exists to remove: the test is registered, the binary is
# never built, and the lane reports on a smaller set than its name
# claims. `BUILDSYSTEM_TARGETS` cannot omit a target defined here.
#
# Placed at the end of the file so every `add_executable` above it has
# already run — a target defined after this block would be missed, which
# is why nothing may be appended below.
get_property(_sce_c_test_targets DIRECTORY PROPERTY BUILDSYSTEM_TARGETS)
add_custom_target(sce_c11_tests
    COMMENT "Building the C11 test surface (ctest -L c11)"
)
foreach(_sce_c_target ${_sce_c_test_targets})
    if(NOT _sce_c_target STREQUAL sce_c11_tests)
        add_dependencies(sce_c11_tests ${_sce_c_target})
    endif()
endforeach()
list(LENGTH _sce_c_test_targets _sce_c_test_target_count)
message(STATUS "sce_c11_tests aggregates ${_sce_c_test_target_count} target(s)")
